# A four-interval tie controller and the finite-chain deformation interface

The arbitrary-chain monotone elimination flow remains unproved. This note gives an exact finite four-fiber continuation, an exact obstruction to equal endpoint-removal rates, and two structural facts that reduce a general interval-chain test to finite rational data. None uses an attained body minimum.

The underlying four-fiber body is archived in `candidate 75dd33535e246a34`. The endpoint-deformation formulas, complete admissible rate cone, and finite continuation below are new consequences of that body. Its all-normal depth at the starting point is not a new result.

## 1. A feasible two-parameter deformation

At bases 0,1,2,3 take

    K0(u)=[47/50+u/2, 26/25-u/2],
    K1=[-11/10,1],
    K2=[-23/25,23/25],
    K3(v)=[-9/100+v/2,9/100-v/2],
    0<=u<=1/10,        0<=v<=9/50.                       (1)

The variables u,v are the masses removed from the two endpoint intervals about their fixed centers. The lower endpoint sequence is convex and the upper endpoint sequence concave: shrinking either extreme interval only relaxes the corresponding endpoint second-difference constraint. Thus every point of the entire rectangle (1) is an actual convex body with these exact sampled fibers. At a vanished endpoint retain its point fiber with one-dimensional volume zero.

Total mixed mass is

    M(u,v)=211/50-u-v.                                  (2)

The exact actual unnormalized maximum depth is

    Q(u,v)=max{Q1(u),Q2(v)},
    Q1(u)=11/10-u/2,       Q2(v)=11/10-v.               (3)

The corresponding deepest candidates are

    Y1(u)=(1,-u/2),          Y2=(2,0).                 (4)

In particular (3) retains the competing source that becomes larger when an unbalanced deformation leaves the source tie.

## 2. A fixed-normal covering certificate for all candidate marks

Use the four actual caps

    x-(z-1)>=-u/2,
    -x-(93/100)(z-1)>=u/2,
    x+2(z-2)>=0,
    -x+2(z-2)>=0.                                     (5)

The first two have mass Q1 and cover every continuous line over z<=1: their margins sum to -(193/100)(z-1). Throughout (1), the first cap contains K0, cuts K1 at -u/2, and misses K2,K3; the second cuts K1 at that same point and misses the other fibers. The strict K2 gaps remain positive even at u=1/10.

The last two have mass Q2 and cover every continuous line over z>=2. Each cuts K2 at zero, contains K3, and misses K0,K1. Consequently (5) bounds the depth of EVERY candidate in every integer fiber by the right side of (3). This is a full-set cover, not a chosen-center estimate.

## 3. Exact all-normal lower certificates throughout the rectangle

For a cap through (p,x), write

    F_p(t)=sum_i clamp(hi_i-x-t(i-p),0,hi_i-lo_i).

Its reverse has mass M-F_p(t). F_p is affine between the finitely many knots t=(lo_i-x)/(i-p),(hi_i-x)/(i-p), i!=p, and constant beyond the outermost knots. Thus its exact minimum and maximum are attained in the following complete knot lists. The knot order shown holds throughout the rectangle (1), with harmless coincident knots at a vanished endpoint.

At p=1, x=-u/2:

| Knot t | F_1(t) |
|---|---:|
| -26/25 | 151/50+u/2-v |
| -47/50-u | 78/25-u/2-v |
| -23/25+u/2 | 78/25-u/2-v |
| (u+v)/4-9/200 | 449/200-u/4-5v/4 |
| (u-v)/4+9/200 | 79/40-u/4+v/4 |
| 23/25+u/2 | 11/10-u/2 |

Every entry lies between Q1 and M-Q1. For example the only potentially tight maximum comparison at the first knot is (M-Q1)-F_1(-26/25)=1/10-u>=0; the remaining comparisons have positive uniform slack or are exact equalities. The far plateaus have the respective outermost knot values. Hence min F_1=Q1 and max F_1=M-Q1.

At p=2, x=0:

| Knot t | F_2(t) |
|---|---:|
| -1 | 11/10-v |
| -13/25+u/4 | 79/50+u/4-v |
| -47/100-u/4 | 173/100-5u/4-v |
| -9/100+v/2 | 211/100-u-v/2 |
| 9/100-v/2 | 211/100-u-v/2 |
| 11/10 | 78/25-u |

Every entry lies between Q2 and M-Q2, with equality on the far plateaus. Pure base caps at either source contain its whole own interval; those interval lengths, 21/10 and 46/25, already exceed Q1,Q2. Thus they do not invalidate either lower certificate. All containing halfspaces contain a parallel through-point cap. This proves (3) for every closed ambient halfspace and every parameter in (1).

## 4. Equal rates fail; a coherent source-tie rate succeeds

Initially beta0=Q(0,0)/M(0,0)=55/211. Equations (2)-(3) give the exact equivalence

    Q(u,v)/M(u,v)<=beta0
    iff 101u>=110v and 156v>=55u.                     (6)

For u=v=t>0, Q=11/10-t/2 and

    beta(t,t)-beta0
      =(9t/100)/[(211/50)(211/50-2t)] > 0.           (7)

Thus simultaneous equal endpoint contraction is genuinely wrong at this full-parity two-source tie, despite actual lattice completeness and a completely regular initial cap menu.

The missing control is the relative rate. Preserve the tie by setting

    v=u/2,      0<=u<=1/10.                          (8)

Both actual source depths then equal 11/10-u/2, while M=211/50-3u/2. The exact derivative is

    d beta/du = -(23/50)/(211/50-3u/2)^2 < 0.        (9)

At the terminal point u=1/10, the left endpoint is a point, the right endpoint still has length13/100, both inner sources remain deepest, and

    Q=21/20,       M=407/100,       beta=105/407.

The removed endpoint was never a deepest source. After removing its zero-mass extreme base, the three remaining positive interval fibers can follow `candidate 44be6cdd33cc2f74` to two equal adjacent fibers. A literal continuous body path can prune the zero endpoint using C_t=C intersect {z>=t}, 0<=t<=1; the positive integer fibers stay unchanged, and the exposed zero fiber has depth zero before it disappears. Therefore this example has a complete finite nonincreasing path, even though the naively symmetric first move goes in the wrong direction.

## 5. Proper critical sections have symmetric consecutive sampled blocks

Let arbitrary positive interval fibers occupy every integer base 0,...,N, with a convex lower roof and concave upper roof. Fix p and a proper cap through Y=(p,y), normalized as x>=y+a(z-p). Suppose its boundary misses every sampled interval endpoint, so its cap mass is differentiable in a. The sampled fibers cut properly by the line form one consecutive block l,...,r containing p.

Indeed the intersection of the line with the interior of the actual convex body is an open line interval. Its base projection is an interval, and its integer points are exactly the properly cut sampled fibers. On a neighborhood of the selected slope,

    d(cap mass)/da = -sum_{i=l}^r(i-p).

At a local minimum over all base tilts this derivative vanishes. Hence

    l+r=2p.                                           (10)

The number of proper sections is therefore odd, and the sampled section block is symmetric about the actual source base. In particular a regular critical cap can cut the right extreme fiber properly only when p>=N/2, and can cut the left extreme properly only when p<=N/2. If it cuts both extremes properly, N must be even and p=N/2.

Equation (10) is a geometric restriction on actual cap data, absent from an arbitrary collection of source gradients. It does not assign arbitrary selectors at supporting endpoints. Such contacts require their actual one-sided chambers; the regular statement alone is insufficient to establish the general flow.

## 6. Exact finite nature of the remaining interval-chain test

For fixed consecutive integer bases, the actual maximum raw depth is a continuous piecewise-linear function of the sampled lower and upper endpoints. Here is a finite reduction, not a convexity assertion.

At a fixed source p and coordinate y, the nonvertical cap mass is piecewise affine in slope a, with knots (lo_i-y)/(i-p),(hi_i-y)/(i-p). Evaluating these finitely many knots and the two far plateaus expresses the upper cap minimum and lower cap minimum as continuous piecewise-linear functions of y and the endpoint parameters. The upper minimum is strictly decreasing in y at rate at least one, because its own-fiber contribution decreases at rate one for every slope; the lower minimum is strictly increasing at rate at least one. Their unique crossing in the own interval gives the actual best mark on that fiber.

On each of the finitely many affine cells, solving this crossing is an affine operation with a nonzero constant rational denominator. Its value is consequently piecewise linear with rational coefficients. Taking the maximum over the finitely many source bases preserves this conclusion. Pure base caps cannot reduce the crossing value: the finite large-slope plateaus already take only the proper own cap together with the same outside side fibers.

Thus every fixed endpoint-contraction proposal admits a finite rational chamber test retaining all source ties and cap switches. What is NOT proved is that the actual chambers always admit a common nonzero pair of endpoint-removal rates, or that those rates can be continued through all subsequent chambers until an endpoint disappears. An arbitrary piecewise-linear maximum does not have that property merely by being finite; (10) is one additional geometric input a proof would need to exploit.

Numerical exploration in `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/search_interval_endpoint_deformation_independent.py` tested 1,500 generic chains, 228 interpolated actual deepest-source ties, and 6,000 centrally symmetric chains with dense or sparse support-roof curvature. No obstruction to some joint endpoint-contraction ratio was found. These floating screens are not certificates of the general flow. The exact result here is the finite four-fiber controller (1)-(9), its equal-rate obstruction, and the structural reductions (10) and Section6.
